newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian Chamber approves party financing law.
newsitem.headline: Italian Chamber approves party financing law.

text.p: Italy's Chamber of Deputies (lower house) on Friday approved new rules on political party financing by a big majority, the second time in a week that opposition parties had voted with the centre-left government.

The new measures, designed to end the sort of illicit funding which was at the heart of the Tangentopoli graft scandals that broke in 1992 bringing down the ruling old guard, now go to the Senate for final approval before they become law.
The bill, setting out how parties may raise money and fixing disclosure rules, passed the Chamber by 422 votes to 13 with 31 abstentions.
The opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance had voted with the government earlier in the week on a package of measures to overhaul the broadcast sector.

The measures did not contain a proposal on decriminalising backdoor political party funding, which was to be the subject of a separate vote on a motion put forward by a Freedom Alliance deputy on Saturday morning.

But Mimmo Luca, vice-chairman of the Democratic Left group in the Chamber, said he was confident the proposal would be opposed, saying it "sets out tomorrow what parliament has shown it refuses to accept today".
Prodi, who opposes an amnesty for past offenders, has made proposals to reform the justice system one of the cornerstones of his 1997 legislative programme.
